title: Protocol to determine the subcellular localization of protein interactions in murine keratinocytes
protocol: Aspirate the growth medium from the tissue culture dish.
Wash the cells three times with ice-cold 1× PBS.
Aspirate the last of PBS.
Add to each dish 800 μL of hypotonic buffer containing protease and phosphatase inhibitor cocktail at a 1× final concentration.
Add DTT to hypotonic buffer to achieve a final concentration of 0.5 mM.
Mix 8 μL of 100× protease and phosphatase inhibitor cocktail with 800 μL hypotonic buffer.
Detach cells from the tissue culture dish using a cell scraper.
Clean the cell scraper with 90% ethanol and air dry before use.
Place the cell suspension in a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube on ice.
Incubate the lysate for 10 min at +4°C on an overhead rotator.
Add IGEPAL CA-630 to a final concentration of 3% (e.g., add 24 μL IGEPAL CA-630 when performing fragmentation with 800 μL hypotonic buffer/lysate).
Vortex the lysate-IGEPAL CA-630 mix well until IGEPAL CA-630 is completely dissolved.
Incubate the lysate for 10 min on ice.
Vortex the lysate-IGEPAL CA-630 mix for 10 s three times during incubation.
Homogenize the cells using hypodermic needles by about ten iterations up and down of the syringe.
Use a syringe with a volume of 1 mL for the indicated buffer volume.
Lysate cells by forcing them through the narrow lumen of the needle.
Subject cells to shear forces upon exit from the needle to induce further lysis.
Apply a small volume of the lysate (1–2 μL) on a slide and check for lysed cells but intact nuclei using a phase-contrast microscope.
Centrifuge lysates for 30 s at 14,000 × g and +4°C to clear lysates.
Collect the supernatant as the cytoplasmic fraction in a new 1.5 mL centrifuge tube kept on ice.
Add 13.3 μL of 4× SDS loading buffer to 40 μL of the cytoplasmic fraction.
Boil lysate at 95°C for 5 min on a heating thermo shaker.
Store the lysates at -20°C until loading the SDS-PAGE gel for immunoblotting.
Wash the pellet three times in hypotonic buffer by centrifugation for 1 min at 14,000 × g and +4°C.
Add protease and phosphatase inhibitor cocktail to hypotonic buffer to achieve a 1× final concentration.
Add DTT to hypotonic buffer to reach a final concentration of 0.5 mM.
Wash the pellet by adding approximately 500 μL of hypotonic buffer and vortexing at low speed until the pellet detaches from the bottom of the centrifuge tube.
Carefully remove the wash hypotonic buffer using a hypodermic needle or pipette tip to avoid losing the pellet.
Add protease and phosphatase inhibitor cocktail to hypertonic buffer to achieve a 1× final concentration.
Add DTT to hypertonic buffer to reach a final concentration of 0.5 mM.
Remove any remaining hypotonic buffer from the pellet.
Add 400 μL of hypertonic buffer containing inhibitors and DTT to each pellet to lyse the nuclei.
Add 4 μL of the 100× protease and phosphatase inhibitor cocktail to 400 μL hypertonic buffer to produce a 1× final concentration.
Add 2 μL of the 100 mM DTT stock solution to 400 μL hypertonic buffer to achieve a final concentration of 0.5 mM.
Incubate the pellet in hypertonic buffer for 30 min at +4°C on an overhead rotator.
Centrifuge the lysate for 30 min at 18,000 × g and +4°C.
Collect the supernatant as the nuclear fraction in a new 1.5 mL centrifuge tube kept on ice.
Mix 40 μL of nuclear fraction with 13.3 μL of 4× SDS loading buffer.
Boil the mixture at 95°C for 5 minutes on a heating thermo shaker.
Store the lysates at -20°C until loading onto a SDS-PAGE gel for immunoblotting.
Keep the remaining volume (360 μL) of nuclear fraction at -20°C for later use or keep it on ice when immediately performing the immunoprecipitation.
Incubate the cytoplasmic and nuclear fraction sample with the appropriate amount of anti-GFP antibody at +4°C on an overhead rotator.
Wash the protein A agarose beads three times in immunoprecipitation buffer.
Add 100 μL of the protein A resin slurry to the cytoplasmic and nuclear fractions containing the preformed antibody-complexes.
Incubate for 4 h at +4°C on an overhead rotator.
Collect and wash the beads by centrifugation.
Discard the supernatant.
Elute the antibody-antigen complex from the resin by adding 70 μL of 1× SDS loading buffer to each sample.
Boil the beads at 95°C for 5 min on a heating thermo shaker.
Store the eluted samples at −20°C until performing SDS-PAGE and immunoblotting.
Incubate the antibody with the cytoplasmic or nuclear fraction sample followed by incubation with appropriate agarose beads to capture protein of interest and its interacting factors.
Keep all solutions and samples on ice to avoid denaturation, proteolysis, or dephosphorylation of proteins.
Thaw the samples of the cytoplasmic and nuclear fraction on ice.
Store the samples on ice to avoid freeze/thaw cycles.
Place appropriate amounts of GFP-Trap Agarose beads in new 1.5 mL centrifuge tubes.
Cut 5 mm from the tip end of pipette tips to minimize loss of beads during pipetting.
Generate a master mix by multiplying the volume of GFP-Trap Agarose bead slurry with the number of samples and adding two more as reserves.
Wash the beads three times in immunoprecipitation buffer by centrifugation for 1 min at 4,000 × g and +4°C.
Add protease and phosphatase inhibitor cocktail to the immunoprecipitation buffer to achieve a final concentration of 1×.
Wash the GFP-Trap Agarose beads by adding immunoprecipitation buffer and vortexing at low speed until the bead pellet detaches from the bottom of the centrifuge tube.
Fully resuspend the beads in immunoprecipitation buffer.
Centrifuge at low speed to avoid crashing the beads.
Remove the immunoprecipitation buffer carefully using a hypodermic needle.
Add immunoprecipitation buffer to the GFP-Trap Agarose beads to achieve a final volume of 100 μL for each 15 μL bead slurry.
Incubate the mixture with cytoplasmic and nuclear fraction samples at +4°C on an overhead rotator for 1 hour.
Collect the agarose beads by centrifugation for 3 minutes at 4,000 × g and +4°C.
Wash the beads three times in immunoprecipitation buffer by centrifugation for 1 minute at 4,000 × g and +4°C.
Remove the immunoprecipitation buffer through a hypodermic needle carefully to avoid losing the pellet.
Add 70 μL of 1× SDS loading buffer to each sample.
Boil the beads at 95°C for 5 minutes on a heating thermo shaker.
Store the samples at −20°C until performing SDS-PAGE and immunoblotting.
Perform SDS-PAGE to separate proteins under denaturing conditions.
Fill the buffer tank with SDS electrophoresis buffer.
Load 15–20 μL of each sample in pockets of the stacking gel.
Load 4 μL of a protein standard in one pocket.
Run the gel with 80 V for 30 min and 100 V for approximately 2–3 h (depending on the size of the gel and acrylamide concentration).
Transfer proteins to a nitrocellulose blotting membrane using Mini Trans-Blot cells for a wet blot approach at 110 V for 70 min.
Stain the membrane in Ponceau S solution for 5 min.
Destain the membrane in ddH2O for 5 min.
Document the stained membrane using a scanner.
Wash the membrane in 1× TBST until completely destained (approximately 3 min).
Block the membrane in 3% skimmed milk/1× TBST or 3% BSA/1× TBST on a rocking shaker for 30 min.
Probe the membrane with the appropriate primary antibody on an overhead rotator at +4°C for 16 h–24 h in a cold room.
Wash membranes in 1× TBST three times for 10 min.
Incubate membranes with the appropriate horseradish peroxidase-conjugated secondary antibody (diluted in 3% skimmed milk/1× TBST) for 1 h.
Wash membranes twice in 1× TBST for 10 min.
Wash membranes once in 1× TBS (without detergent) for 10 min.
Treat membranes with enhanced chemiluminescence western blotting substrate (equal parts chemiluminescence solution 1 and 2) or ultra-sensitive substrate from a company.
Detect signals using an imaging system.
